concepts.why: The patient has a small, pearly lesion in the tear trough region of the left lower eyelid, which is consistent with basal cell carcinoma, and the pathology report confirms nodular BCC.

The patient has contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue and increased scleral show, which are signs of cicatricial entropion, and the examination notes cicatricial effects causing conjunctival shrinkage and eyelid skin contracture.

The patient's ocular prosthesis would spontaneously extrude from his anophthalmic socket, which is a complication of ocular prosthesis, and the examination notes increased scleral show and shortening of the lower eyelid skin.

The patient has a history of traumatic icicle injury and subsequent surgeries, which can lead to anophthalmic socket contracture, and the examination notes contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue and shortening of the lower eyelid skin.
It explains the infiltrative pattern with no signs of fibrosis or inflammatory infiltrate found in the pathology report.
